Raj: One quick clarification from the live Q&A: when we pitch "serving as the moat," what is the single sentence we want AEs to use vs customers who ask about model coverage?

Elena (CEO): Use this: "We turn model capability into predictable outcomes — stable latency, transparent unit costs, and enterprise controls across hosted, dedicated, or private deployments." Keep it outcomes-first, not model-first.

Naomi (PMM): For marketing, should we lead with numbers or keep high level?

Marco (Head Strategy): Internally: always use p50/p95/p99 plus workload profile. Externally: conservative, contextual numbers only. Example: short-chat p99 = 120ms (95th percentile workload described).

Felix (Eng): Technical nuance: when quoting p99, call out whether caching and batching were enabled. That materially changes the baseline.

Cassie (CS): Customers keep asking "why not just self-host?" Short rebuttal for CS playbook?

Elena (CEO): Rebuttal: self-host hides significant ops and tuning cost. Our value is predictable economics, maintained fallbacks, and operational guardrails so features actually ship and stay healthy.

Raj (AE): AE asks: competitor line vs cloud vendor who touts global infra and model catalogs?

Marco (Head Strategy): Positioning line: Cloud vendor = scale + model breadth; our pitch = unified runtime + measurable economics + deployment flexibility. Simple and factual.

Naomi (PMM): Can we get a one-paragraph elevator for the website that avoids "best models" language?

Elena (CEO): Draft: "Redwood Inference makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical to run—stable latency, transparent costs, and enterprise controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Felix (Eng): Ops/roadmap question: does this shift mean more work on observability vs integrating additional model families?

Elena (CEO): Roadmap tilt: invest first in serving primitives that scale (observability, smart routing, caching, rollout controls). Model integrations continue, but they are enabled by a stronger serving layer.

Cassie (CS): Actionable ask: Sales & CS want a short FAQ rebuttal doc for self-host vs Redwood — can Product produce it?

Naomi (PMM): Yes. I'll draft a 1-pager: 3 bullets for value, 2 tech substantiation points, and 2 quick customer stories. Target Fri EOD.

Marco (Head Strategy): Also recommend a two-slide appendix for AEs: 1) 30s opener + 3 bullets, 2) tech appendix mapping scenario->config (short/chat vs long/context).

Raj (AE): Can Solutions get a tech appendix showing concrete configs (batching, quant, cache) and expected percent savings? They asked for numbers to send to prospects.

Felix (Eng): We'll provide a short table and conservative savings ranges by Wed: short-chat (20-50%), long-context (15-40%) assuming caching + batching.

Elena (CEO): Good. Summarize action items: 1) @Naomi draft FAQ + one-pager by Fri. 2) @Felix produce tech appendix + conservative savings by Wed. 3) @Marco assemble AE two-slide pack by Thu. I'll review before publish. :thumbsup:

all-hands-bot: Thanks everyone — recording, slides, and follow-ups will be posted to #all-hands-resources.
